Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
120 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No changes to watches warnings or advisories with this update.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A storm system impacts the area Thanksgiving into Friday 
with rain and strong to damaging winds.

2) Widespread moderate coastal flooding likely during this AM 
and PM high tides, with locally major possible mainly for 
southern Nassau and southwest Suffolk. Minor to locally moderate
impacts possible during Friday AM high tide. In addition, 
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion expected along the 
open water shorelines during the times of high tide, with 
localized overwashes possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Low pressure center to our south tracks north today and passes to 
our west late tonight into early Friday morning. A secondary low 
pressure center or triple point approaches and passes through or 
close to Long Island late tonight. An anomalously strong high over 
the Northeast into Canadian Maritimes will help create a strong 
pressure gradient, and this combined with a strong low level jet 
passing through, will help produce strong to damaging winds across 
the forecast area today into tonight. Some rain impacts are possible 
as well.

Regarding winds, there is still some disagreement among the guidance 
regarding how quickly the low level jet and triple point pass 
through the region. For this reason, timing of the Wind Advisories 
and High Wind Warnings have been unchanged. There is at least high 
enough confidence that the timing of the strongest winds are most 
likely to occur from late this afternoon into this evening.
Cannot completely rule out a few gusts to 50kt across coastal 
CT and Southern Westchester County with funneling effects from 
the adjacent LI Sound. on an ENE wind. Did not expand the 
Warning farther inland into NE NJ as guidance generally does not
support a likelihood of widespread warning conditions. With 
that said, perhaps Eastern Bergen County could have isolated 
gusts of 50kt+. The Wind Advisory, particularly over western 
portions of the forecast area, is perhaps posted for too long of
a time, but impacts should be felt at least into the evening 
hours. 

As for the rainfall, overall amounts haven't changed much from the 
previous forecast. Guidance still suggests that the heaviest 
rainfall is most likely to occur late this afternoon into evening. A 
rumble of thunder also cannot be ruled out during the evening hours. 
Impacts should be limited to minor/poor drainage flooding. Still a 
slight chance that flash flood thresholds are met in the NYC metro, 
but a mitigating factor will be the quick motion of the heavier 
cells.

Rain coverage and wind speeds diminish late tonight. Light rainfall 
still a possibility, especially north and west of the city during 
Friday with surface low pressure still nearby and an upper low and 
cold pool aloft. High pressure then slowly builds in with dry 
weather across the area for Saturday.

.KEY MESSAGE 2...
With a recent full moon, astronomical tides remain 
rather high and many locations need less than a foot to reach minor 
coastal flood benchmarks with the AM high tides and closer to 2 ft 
with the PM high tides.

A period of gale to storm force ENE winds will affect the region 
this morning into tonight. The region remains between an approaching 
low pressure and strong high pressure to the north. This will bring 
the likelihood for widespread moderate coastal flooding with this AM 
and PM high tides, with potential for major coastal flooding along 
the western Great South Bay. Other areas of notes for significant 
impacts will be the Peconic Bay area with funneling of surge towards 
the Peconic River, and along W LI Sound shoreline with moderate 
water levels combined with high wave action. Surge up the tidally 
affected rivers (Hackensack, Hudson, and Passaic) will result in 
minor to moderate flooding as well.

There have been no changes to the Coastal Flood 
Watch/Warning/Advisories through Friday, but expected surge now 
lines up better with this evening's high tide cycle. Widespread 
minor to moderate coastal flooding is still expected with this 
morning's high tide, but this evening's high tide will now likely be 
the higher of the two. This is especially true for locations along 
the Long Island Sound.

The forecast has been leaned to a blend of 75th percentile of 
Stevens SFAS and NAEFS P-ETSS (good middle ground btwn ECMWF and 
GEFS PETSS) with deterministic ETSS/STOFS. The lean towards the 
higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin.

For the Friday AM high tides, winds switch to the southwest. Still 
can not completely rule out some areas locally touching moderate 
along the south shore of Long Island, but confidence in this has 
lowered as guidance has come in quite a bit lower. Have left the 
Coastal Flood Watch up for now given some uncertainty.

For the oceanfront, breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result in 
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high 
tide. There is potential for localized overwashes, exacerbating 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective 
dunes. Along Western LI Sound and Twin Forks, breaking waves of 3 to 
6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. 
Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable 
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential 
for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well.

Heavy rain coinciding with the Thursday evening high tides could 
exacerbate street flooding issues along the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
**HIGH IMPACT STORM TODAY AND TONIGHT**

A large storm will continue to move across the Mid Atlantic 
states today passing to the W late tonight. An associated warm 
front will approach this evening. 

MVFR cigs have developed across NYC metros and along the coast
with IFR conditions expected as rain becomes moderate to heavy 
at times this afternoon.

Winds out of the NE-ENE will increase into the afternoon to 
25-35 kt with G40- 50kt, strongest at the NYC metro and coastal 
terminals. Peak wind gusts could be a few kt higher. This will 
also be accompanied by easterly LLWS at 50-70kt at 1500-2000 ft 
AGL.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of strongest winds and heaviest rain timing could be off
a few hours.

Isolated thunder can not be ruled out this evening.


.OUTLOOK FOR 18Z Friday through Tuesday... 

Friday: Chance of showers with MVFR cond, becoming VFR at 
night. SW winds G25-30kt, becoming W after midnight. 

Saturday: VFR. W winds G20-25kt, diminishing at night. 

Sunday: VFR.

Sunday night: Showers likely with MVFR cond after midnight. 

Monday: Chance of morning showers with MVFR cond. SW winds G20-25kt, 
becoming W in the afternoon and NW at night.

Tuesday: VFR. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
No changes to the Gale and Storm Warnings. Seas on the ocean are 
modeled to build to around 20 ft at the height of the storm in the 
late aftn and eve, with waves on the Sound and the NY Harbor 
entrance up to around 10 ft. 

Conditions improve a little on Fri, but a SW gale is likely on 
the ocean and maybe on some of the non-ocean waters as well.  
Winds diminish to SCA lvls on Sat, and likely blw SCA lvls on 
Sun. A frontal sys on Mon could produce SCA conditions,
especially on the ocean.
